title: Height-Balanced Indexing for Secure Tar Extraction in the Aether-Flux Ecosystem
topic: A fast and secure tar parser for the Aether-Flux ecosystem
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Tar archives are ubiquitous in distributed systems, yet their extraction remains a source of security vulnerabilities and performance bottlenecks. We present a Python parser that constructs a height-balanced binary search tree over entry names, enabling $O(\log N)$ lookup and insertion while enforcing strict path-sanitization invariants. The parser operates on raw 512-byte blocks, validates checksums, and rejects entries that would traverse outside the intended extraction root. Formal analysis demonstrates that the tree remains strictly height-balanced after each insertion, guaranteeing logarithmic search time. Static Abstract Syntax Tree inspection confirms a structural complexity of $O(N)$ auxiliary memory and a balanced-tree depth bound of $\lceil \log_2(N+1) \rceil$. No runtime benchmarks were performed; all claims are supported by static analysis and formal proofs. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261027_230150_a_fast_and_secure_tar_parser_f}.
